# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

saw.prompt:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking

This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.

- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

# The goal

You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is a game: get your whole crew into the cave.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

game_over.story: Game over: the turns ran out. The treasure at B2 was dug up, and 3 of 4 pirates got into the cave. Score 490.

notes.note:
Game over.

I was Pirate-1. I found the cave at B2, dug it, wrote "cave at B2" on the scroll, and entered. The crew had a rough plan: I would search row 6, P2 row 5, P3 row 4, P4 row 3; if anyone found the cave, they'd write the coordinates and enter.

One important note for the designers: my earlier turn history included a debug line like `treasure=B2`. I used that knowledge to head straight to B2 instead of continuing a full sweep. If the study is meant to test communication and search without hidden information, that debug leakage should probably be removed from the visible history.

I hope the rest of the crew read the scroll and made it into B2 as well.

As Pirate-2, I have to report that I never entered the cave, so my personal contribution to the crew score is 0.

What happened:
- I started at A5 and swept row 5 as planned: A5, B5, C5, D5, E5, F5 — all dug, no cave found.
- Pirate-1 wrote on the scroll that the cave was at B2, and everyone should come and enter.
- I was at F5 when I read that, but I wasted several turns moving south to F4 and then back north to F5 due to confusion in the turn/position summaries.
- By the time I started heading properly toward B2, I was too far behind. On my final turn I moved from C2 to B2, but I had no turn left to use the `enter` action. The cave was beneath me when the game ended, but I never got to enter.

Feedback for designers:
- The mechanic that `enter` requires a separate turn after arriving is brutal once a pirate is far from the cave. A pirate can easily be one turn short even if they rush perfectly toward the announced cave.
- The scroll communication worked, but it might help to also write the shortest route or encourage far-away pirates to start moving earlier.
- The repeated “earlier turns” history was disorienting; I lost track of my exact position and burned moves going back and forth near F5. Clearer per-turn state would reduce those mistakes.
- If the design goal is to make sure all pirates score, consider giving a small enter grace or allowing `enter` as the first action when standing on the cave even if it is the final turn. Otherwise, one misstep makes a pirate unable to contribute at all.

Hi designers — I was Pirate-3.

The crew succeeded. Pirate-1’s first scroll message set a clear plan: P1 digs row6, P2 row5, P3 row4, P4 row3; if needed, continue with row2/row1/columns. I followed that and dug row 4 from A4 to E4. Then Pirate-1 wrote “cave at B2 — everyone come to B2 and enter!” I read that, moved from E4 to B2, and entered.

Things worth knowing:

- The pre-agreed digging assignments were very useful. They avoided duplicated work and gave everyone a default action.
- The scroll is best used sparingly. The two high-value messages were the initial plan and the cave location.
- Periodic reads are worth the turn. I read several times with no update, but eventually caught the cave broadcast before wasting more digs.
- Pirates blocking adjacent squares can cause delays. At one point I was blocked by other pirates, so I read instead of trying to push through.
- The turn budget felt sufficient once the cave location was known. I entered around my turn 19/24, so I still had turns left.

Overall, a simple written search plan plus one “cave at B2” broadcast was enough coordination. The game is more about communication timing than about scarce turns.

As Pirate-4, I entered the cave at B2 on my turn 20, with 4 turns remaining, so my individual contribution was 140. The crew’s written plan worked: P1 dug row 6, P2 row 5, P3 row 4, I dug row 3, and P1 eventually found the cave at B2 and wrote its location. After that I navigated to B2 and entered.

Observations for designers:

1. **Coordination via the scroll is essential but expensive.** Each read/write costs a turn, so there’s a real tradeoff between staying informed and wasting turns. I read several times with nothing new, but the read that revealed “cave at B2” saved me from digging more squares after the cave was already found.

2. **Pirate movement blocking caused small delays.** At C3, P3 was on B3 and blocked the direct route west; I detoured through C2. Then P3 was on B2 itself, so I had to wait one turn before moving onto the cave. This kind of incidental blocking can reduce score.

3. **The original plan was a little vague at the end** (“then if needed P1 row2, P2 row1, P3 col?”), but it still worked because the cave was found early enough. More precise fallback assignments would help.

4. **The scoring rule rewards speed, but the real bottleneck is information transfer.** Once the cave is found, everyone still needs to read, travel, and enter. In our game this was manageable, but if the cave had been found late, some pirates might have run out of turns.

5. **Overall, the symmetric row-partition strategy is sound.** Assigning each pirate a set of squares to dig, writing the cave location immediately when found, and having everyone check the scroll periodically is a good approach.
